If θ ≥ 0, both (−1,0) and (1,1) lie strictly within the v-strip: their absolute v-projections relative to the center are at most 3/(2√2) and 1, respectively, both less than L/2. To avoid adding interior lattice points, they must therefore lie beyond opposite u-sides. This requires L ≤ 2cos θ + sin θ ≤ √5, a contradiction. If θ < 0, the same argument uses (0,−1) and (1,1) beyond opposite v-sides, again giving L ≤ √5. Thus the bound is universal and attained, matching both proposed scopes.
